<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def ballpos():
    for n in current_frame.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['color']=='N':
            b=n['boundary']; return (min(p[0] for p in b),min(p[1] for p in b))
    return None
# BFS: explore reachable positions
from collections import deque
start=ballpos()
print("start:",start)
visited={start}
q=deque([start])
moves={'UP':(-2,0),'DOWN':(2,0),'LEFT':(0,-2),'RIGHT':(0,2)}
order=['UP','DOWN','LEFT','RIGHT']
# We'll do a limited BFS by actually moving. To save actions, first map by trying each dir once per node.
# Do a simple expansion: for each visited node, try all 4 dirs once, record new positions.
# We'll physically move to each node then back. This is expensive; instead do a "star" probe from start.
# Probe: from start, go far in each dir, then back.
import json
# Just record the 4 extreme positions by pushing far in each dir then returning.
res={}
for d in order:
    p=ballpos()
    for _ in range(10):
        action([d]); np=ballpos()
        if np==p: break
        p=np
    res[d]=p
    # return to start
    back={'UP':'DOWN','DOWN':'UP','LEFT':'RIGHT','RIGHT':'LEFT'}[d]
    for _ in range(12):
        action([back]); np=ballpos()
        if np==start: break
print("extremes:",res)
print("back at:",ballpos())
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
